correctness.rationale: The regular-direction Gram matrix has all off-diagonal entries -1/d; from equal squared distances to the circumcenter and the relation sum_i v_i=0 one obtains common tau=B/U and 2(c·v_i)=r_i-mu/r_i. Using S=sum lambda_i r_i and sum lambda_i=1 yields lambda_i=[d+kappa w_i-d mu w_i^2]/[2(d+1)] with mu=B/U, kappa=[(d+1)(2-d)+d mu sum w_i^2]/U. This is a downward quadratic with f(0)>0 and a single positive root, giving negative barycentric coordinates exactly for an initial block of smallest radii, including ties. Normalize r_[2]=1 and x=r_[2]/r_[1] to obtain U>=d+x, B<=d+1/x, and V-U>=-x(1-x); substituting gives lambda_[2]>=1/(2d)+[(d-1)(d+1)x^2]/[2d(d+x)^2], with equality if and only if all but the possibly largest radius agree. This forces two positive coordinates; k small radii vs d+1-k very large radii realizes exactly k negative coordinates, k=0,..,d-1. 1,200 independently solved circumcenters in dimensions 2–9 confirm both formula and lower bound; no inference of all-dimension truth from random tests.
residual_risks: Full dimension d>=2 and r_i>0 only; limiting equality at infinite radius is an unattained infimum.
